children.name: Trichoplax
children.description: Trichoplax adhaerens is a small, flattened, multicellular animal a few millimetres across with no organs, muscles, or nervous system. It can regenerate from any body fragment.

children.name: Trichoplax adhaerens
children.description: The first placozoan species discovered (1883). A tiny, flattened disc of cells that glides over surfaces by ciliary motion and feeds by engulfing algae and microbes. Found in warm coastal waters worldwide.

children.name: Treptoplax
children.description: A dubious genus described in 1896 from the Mediterranean, never observed again. Likely synonymous with Trichoplax.

children.name: Treptoplax reptans
children.description: Described from the Mediterranean in 1896. Never re-discovered. Considered a nomen dubium by most placozoan researchers.
